objects.description: Millisecond-precision time quantity. Intended for time-difference calculations rather than absolute wall-clock time. It is an alias of unsigned int; range and wraparound behavior depend on platform width of unsigned int.

functions.name: time_get_millis
functions.description: Returns the current time value in millisecond precision as a time_millis (typedef of unsigned int). Intended primarily for computing time differences rather than as an absolute timestamp. Because the underlying type is an unsigned int, callers should expect wrap-around over long runtimes and design difference calculations accordingly.
requirements: Use the returned value only for time-difference calculations; do not treat it as a stable/absolute wall-clock timestamp.
Handle potential wrap-around of the unsigned int value when computing differences (e.g., modular arithmetic).
No explicit initialization requirements are documented for calling this function.

functions.name: time_set_millis
functions.description: Sets the current time value (in milliseconds) used by the time subsystem. Typically useful for testing or environments where the clock is controlled. The value is stored as time_millis (unsigned int), consistent with time_get_millis.
requirements: Parameter millis must be a time_millis value representing milliseconds (unsigned int).
Be aware that subsequent calls to time_get_millis will reflect this set value; design tests accordingly.
No explicit range constraints beyond the limits of time_millis are documented; wrap-around behavior follows unsigned int semantics.
